info.title: Power Platform Admin Analytics API (CS Analytics)
info.description:
The Power Platform admin analytics API manages tenant-level analytics data exports — the connections that push Power Platform telemetry into a customer-owned data sink.

There is no single host: analytics is served from **regional** hosts, and a caller must first discover its tenant's region through the Power Platform API's `gateway/cluster` lookup, then address the matching regional host. A request to the wrong region succeeds and silently returns an incomplete answer.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/analytics) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

x-region-hosts.description: geoName (from `GET /gateway/cluster`, compared case-insensitively) -> analytics host. Commercial entries give the `region` server-variable value; sovereign entries give a full host, because those sit on different domains.

notes.emea: Europe, Middle East and Africa — the catch-all European geography, distinct from the single-country European hosts below.
notes.au: Australia. Live-observed geoName, and **absent from the Terraform provider's map**, which is why its analytics data source fails on Australian tenants. There is no `au` host; `oce` serves it.
notes.pac: Asia Pacific. Note the geoName and the host prefix differ.
notes.ch: Switzerland. Alternate geoName spelling carried by the Terraform provider; unattested in a live response.
notes.sgp: Singapore. Shares a physical cluster with `apac` but is a separate deployment.
notes.pol: Poland. Host live-verified; **absent from the Terraform provider's map**.
notes.ita: Italy. Host live-verified; **absent from the Terraform provider's map**.
notes.dod: US Department of Defense. Note the different domain — and see `x-provider-defects` for the malformed hostname the Terraform provider ships.

x-verification-legend.host: the host answered GET /api/v2/connections with 200 on 2026-08-27
x-verification-legend.geo: this geoName was observed in a live gateway/cluster response
x-verification-legend.reachable: the host answered, but rejects a commercial-cloud token, so its paths were not probed

x-provider-defects: `internal/clients/analytics/data_exports.go` maps DOD to `dod.csanalytics.csanalytics.appsplatform.us`, doubling the `csanalytics` label. That name does not resolve (NXDOMAIN); the real host is `dod.csanalytics.appsplatform.us`, which answers. Corrected here.

The provider's map has no key for geoName `au`, which is what a live Australian tenant returns, so its analytics data source fails with `invalid region: au` before issuing a request. `oce` serves that tenant. Added here.
The provider's map lacks the live `pol` (Poland) and `ita` (Italy) hosts. Added here.

The provider upper-cases the geoName before lookup while the service returns it lower-case. Its map keys are upper-case so this works, but it means an unmapped geography fails hard rather than degrading.

x-notes.note:
Most of this spec is read out of the Power Platform admin centre's own JavaScript bundles. Three things follow that a reader should hold onto.

**`adminanalytics` is a different service from `csanalytics`**, on its own host, and csanalytics names it as its own authorization endpoint. Both take the same geo short-code prefix.

**The bundles do not contain hostnames at the call sites.** They build `https://csanalytics/api/...` where `csanalytics` is a *service alias key*, swapped for a real endpoint by a request interceptor against a per-ring table. Anyone reading these bundles will otherwise attribute routes to the wrong host -- which is exactly what happened while this spec was being written, putting the `/api/v1/cds/*` reports on csanalytics when they belong to adminanalytics.

**A bundle shows what the client *can* send, not what the service accepted.** Every query parameter and body field here is one the code is capable of setting, including on branches no session reached. That makes the coverage wider than a capture and the confirmation weaker: nothing sourced this way is `x-probe-verified`.

The geo prefix is derived differently by different clients, and the answers need not agree. This spec's `x-region-hosts` maps the `geoName` from `GET /gateway/cluster`. The admin centre instead reads `GET /providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/tenant?api-version=2020-08-01` and takes `defaultEnvironmentGeo`, falling back to `dataStorageGeo`, then maps that through a 24-entry table. A tenant whose default environment sits outside its data-storage geography would resolve to different hosts by the two routes.

servers.description: Commercial cloud. Pick `region` by resolving the caller's `geoName` through `info.x-region-hosts`; every value in the enum was confirmed to serve `GET /api/v2/connections`.

region.description: Regional host prefix. **Not always the geoName**: an Australian tenant reports geoName `au` and is served by `oce`, and a `pac` tenant by `apac`. Sovereign clouds are separate `servers` entries because they use different domains.

servers.description: US Government Community Cloud. Reachable; not probed with a matching token.
US Government GCC High. Reachable; not probed with a matching token.

tags.name: Data Export
tags.description: Exporting Dataverse and Power Platform telemetry to a customer-owned sink.

tags.name: Data Export Connections
tags.description: A data-export connection is the tenant-level object behind *Data export* in the Power Platform admin center: it binds a set of environments to one Azure sink (an Application Insights component) and streams a chosen set of telemetry scenarios into it, reporting ingestion health per scenario. Connections are created and edited in the admin center UI; this API only reads them back.

get.description: Default settings for a geography, used to seed a tenant that has none of its own.

post.description: Creates a data-export connection from a set of environments to a destination sink. The body names the source, the environments by both `environmentId` and `organizationId`, and the sink by its Azure subscription and resource group.

delete.description: Removes a data-export connection. Note the segment order differs from v2.

get.description: Which resources the tenant has marked important, as a map of ARM resource type to resource ids.

post.description: Marks resources important. The body is a map keyed by a **normalised** resource type -- `microsoft.powerplatform/environments` becomes `environments`, `microsoft.copilotstudio/agents` becomes `copilotstudio` -- rather than by the full ARM type.

delete.description: Unmarks resources. **This DELETE carries a JSON request body**, in the same shape as the POST. Many generated clients cannot send one, and many proxies drop it.

get.description: Whether the tenant has consented to the analytics data flow. Observed answering **204 with no body** on every one of eleven calls in a session where consent had not been given -- so a client must treat 204 as 'no consent recorded' rather than as an error or as an empty success. The portal re-asks on each navigation rather than caching the answer.

204.description: No consent has been recorded for the tenant. Not an error.

get.description: Reads one tenant setting, addressed by key in the path rather than by a query parameter. `tenantconsent` is one such key.

delete.description: Removes a tenant setting. Note the verb appears in the path as well as in the method.

post.description: Writes one tenant setting. The body carries the acting `userId` alongside the value, so the service records who consented rather than inferring it from the token.

get.description:
Returns every data-export connection the caller's geography holds for the tenant, wrapped in a `{ "value": [...] }` envelope. There is no `@odata` metadata, no `nextLink` and no paging; `$top`, `$filter` and every other query parameter are accepted and ignored, so the response is always the full set.

**Resolve the host before calling this.** Results are scoped to the geography the host serves, and a valid token is accepted on *every* regional host, so an unresolved guess succeeds and returns the wrong geography's (usually empty) list. Call *Region Discovery* first, take `geoName` from its response and index `info.x-region-hosts`.

The path is read-only: there is no create, update or delete operation on this surface. Connections are configured in the admin center under *Data export*.

Each connection's sink carries its Application Insights instrumentation key in plain text, so treat the whole response body as a credential.

Service-principal tokens do not work against this API; call it with user authentication.

200.description: The tenant's data-export connections in this geography. An empty `value` is normal and ambiguous — it means either that nothing is configured or that this host serves a geography the tenant does not use, so confirm the region before reading it as "none configured".

empty.summary: No connections configured — the live-probed result

post.description: The v2 form of sink connection creation. Its `resourceProvider` values are **space-containing strings** -- `cloud flow`, `customer service`, `dataverse`, `power apps` -- rather than identifiers, and two sink fields (`vnetEnabled`, `connectionString`) are attached only when a feature check passes.

delete.description: The v2 delete. The same three identifiers appear in a different order and under a different segment name (`connection` rather than `ids`), so the two versions are not path-compatible.

servers.description: The tenant-scoped Power Platform API host. The label is the tenant GUID with hyphens stripped, split so the final two characters form their own label.

tenantPrefix.description: The tenant GUID without hyphens, less its final two characters — 30 characters.

tenantSuffix.description: The final two characters of the tenant GUID without hyphens.

get.description: Returns the Power Platform cluster serving the caller, whose `geoName` selects the analytics host through `info.x-region-hosts`. This is a PPAPI operation: it lives on the tenant-scoped `api.powerplatform.com` host and takes the Power Platform API scope, not the analytics one — note the per-operation `servers` and `security` overrides.

x-notes.note: The tenant GUID in the host is decorative. A bogus tenant label, and the bare `api.powerplatform.com` host carrying no tenant label at all, both return the caller's own cluster: the answer comes from the bearer token, not from the host.
`api-version` is optional and ignored. Omitting it, or passing `2`, returns the same body as `api-version=1`.

analytics_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The analytics hosts accept tokens for the admin-analytics audience only; a valid Power Platform API token is rejected.

ppapi_auth.description: Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2 for the Power Platform API, used only by the region-discovery operation.

Unauthorized.description: The token was rejected at the gateway, before the service saw the request. The body is `text/plain`, not JSON, and takes one of three forms: empty, with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="invalid_token"`, when no `Authorization` header was sent; `MISE unauthorized.` for a malformed bearer; and `An error occurred processing your authentication.` for a well-formed token issued for the wrong audience — the last is the one to check first, since the analytics hosts reject Power Platform API tokens.

enum: An error occurred processing your authentication.
schema.x-enum-evidence: The three bodies observed on 2026-08-27; the gateway may emit others.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Sent only when the request carried no `Authorization` header.

Forbidden.description: The token is valid for this audience but the caller is not a tenant administrator. Only tenant administrators may read data-export connections.

NotFound.description: No such route. The body is empty: the service returns no error document for unknown paths. `/api/v2/connections/{id}` answers this way, so there is no per-connection read — fetch the list and filter it.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The connections paths are read-only. Every method other than `GET` — including `OPTIONS` and `HEAD` — is refused this way, with an `Allow` header naming `GET` alone.

ConnectionListResponse.description: The listing envelope. Live-verified: `value` is its only member, with no paging cursor and no `@odata` metadata alongside it.

value.description: Every data-export connection in this geography, unordered and unpaged.

Connection.description:
One data-export connection: a set of environments streaming a set of telemetry scenarios into one Azure sink.

Note what is *not* here — there is no schedule, frequency or retention field. Export cadence is fixed by the service and is not caller-configurable; the only timing signal a connection exposes is each scenario's `lastRunOn`.

source.description: The integration that produced this connection — which admin-center feature created it. Distinct from `resourceProvider`, which names the Power Platform service whose telemetry is being exported.
source.x-enum-evidence: Single value observed in the provider's recorded admin-center fixture; the set may be larger.

environments.description: The environments whose telemetry this connection exports. One connection covers many environments, and an environment may appear in more than one connection, so this is not a partition.

status.description: Ingestion health, one entry per exported scenario — each entry's `name` matches a member of `scenarios`. Health is reported per scenario, not per connection, so a connection can be healthy for some streams and stalled for others.

packageName.description: The analytics package — the named bundle of scenarios — the connection was created from. Set by the admin center at configuration time and not otherwise meaningful to a caller.

scenarios.description: The telemetry streams this connection exports. Carried as UI display strings rather than stable codes (`Plugin executions excep` is a truncated label, not an identifier), so match them to `status[].name` rather than treating them as an API vocabulary.

resourceProvider.description: The Power Platform service emitting the telemetry. Despite the name this is not an Azure resource-provider namespace — the observed value is the lower-case service name `dataverse`.
resourceProvider.x-enum-evidence: Single value observed in the provider's recorded admin-center fixture; the set may be larger.

aiType.description: How the Application Insights resource is attached. `Local` means the customer supplied their own component in their own subscription — the only arrangement the admin center's data-export UI offers.
aiType.x-enum-evidence: Single value observed in the provider's recorded admin-center fixture; the set may be larger.

ConnectionEnvironment.description: One environment in a connection's scope, identified twice over: telemetry is emitted against the Dataverse organization, while everything else in Power Platform addresses the environment, so both ids are carried.

organizationId.description: The Dataverse organization id of the environment, which is what appears in the exported telemetry. Environments without Dataverse have none and cannot be exported from.

ConnectionStatus.description: Ingestion health for a single exported scenario within a connection.

name.description: The scenario this entry reports on; matches an entry in the connection's `scenarios`.

state.description: Whether the exporter is attached and delivering for this scenario. `Connected` is the healthy state.
state.x-enum-evidence: Single value observed in the provider's recorded admin-center fixture; failure states exist but were not captured.

lastRunOn.description: When this scenario last exported. With no schedule field on a connection, this is the only freshness signal a caller gets: a `lastRunOn` far in the past is how a stalled export shows up. Serialised in the .NET round-trip form — a numeric UTC offset and seven fractional-second digits — not the `Z`-suffixed form other Power Platform APIs use.

message.description: Explanatory text for a non-healthy `state`. Sent as an explicit `null`, not omitted, when there is nothing to report.

Sink.description: The Azure destination a connection writes telemetry into — in practice a customer-owned Application Insights component, which is then queried like any other Application Insights data.

id.description: The sink's full ARM resource id, and the authoritative locator: `subscriptionId` and `resourceGroupName` merely restate parts of it and are not always sent, so parse this when you need them reliably.

type.description: The kind of destination, which determines how the remaining sink fields are read. `AppInsights` is an Application Insights component addressed by instrumentation key.
type.x-enum-evidence: Single value observed in the provider's recorded admin-center fixture and its DTO; the data-export feature offers no other destination today.

subscriptionId.description: Azure subscription holding the sink. Optional: it can be absent even though `id` contains it.

resourceGroupName.description: Resource group holding the sink. Optional: it can be absent even though `id` contains it.

resourceName.description: Name of the Application Insights component; the last segment of `id`.

key.description: The Application Insights instrumentation key the exporter writes with. This is a live credential returned in plain text by an unprivileged-looking list call — do not log the response, and rotate the key if it leaks.

GatewayCluster.description: The Power Platform cluster serving a tenant. Its `geoName` is the key that selects an analytics host. Live-verified: all seven members were present.

clusterNumber.description: Zero-padded ordinal of the cluster within its geography — a string, not a number.

geoName.description: Short geography code, lower-case, and **not** an Azure region name. This is the key into `info.x-region-hosts`; several codes do not match their host prefix (`au` -> `oce`, `pac` -> `apac`).
geoName.x-enum-evidence: `au` was observed live; `us` appears in the Terraform provider's recorded fixture; the remainder are the keys of the provider's host map, which the provider documents as gateway-cluster geo names. The set may be incomplete — treat an unknown code as a missing host-table entry, not as an error.

environment.description: Service ring the cluster belongs to. Unrelated to a Power Platform environment.

clusterType.description: Role of the cluster within the ring.

clusterCategory.description: Broad classification of the cluster; in the observed response it repeats `environment`.

clusterName.description: Internal cluster identifier, encoding ring, type, number and Azure region — `prdcm001eau` is production customer-management cluster 001 in East Australia. Useful for correlating with the `x-ms-islandgateway` response header.

geoLongName.description: Lower-case long geography name, matching the `location` an environment reports.
